_: The precorneal tear film AS A STRUCTURE on the eye: ~50 nm lipid over ~3.3 um aqueous-mucin over the glycocalyx, with menisci at the lid margins. It is the lubricant of the lid wiper and the optical front surface. Fluid properties are those of `tears` (fluids lane); this profile holds the film's own geometry, lubrication and dynamics. Eye-and-hair materials lane, 2026-11-07.

thin_film.v: lipid 52.7 nm x 1.48 = 78 nm optical path: weak interference colour; 100-150 nm patches tint

kinetic.src: CHEN26 porcine lid-eyeball; WILSON15 via CHEN26

friction.counterface: what the film lubricates (lid wiper on cornea/conjunctiva)

regime.v: boundary to (elasto)hydrodynamic along the Stribeck curve: boundary at blink start/end (low speed), mixed/EHL mid-blink (~100+ mm/s)
regime.src: CHEN26 / LIEVENS22 reviews; Jones 2008 EHL of the lid wiper (via CHEN26)

water_contact_angle_deg.src: aqueous on its own mucin glycocalyx spreads (film forms)

phase.src: a liquid film; in a rigid-body/cloth solver represent it as the lubricated interface (pair friction 0.05), not as particles

model.v: incompressible thin film: squeezed to the lid-wiper gap (sub-micron) under 1-10 kPa; carries load hydrodynamically mid-blink
model.src: Reynolds lubrication with the values above

wave_speed_m_s.src: sqrt(2 pi gamma/(rho lambda)) with gamma 0.044 N/m, lambda 1 mm

volume_uL.src: MISHIMA66 via tears.json: E: recalled from Mishima 1966 (~7 uL), not re-read

breakup.src: dry spots: highlight breaks up; friction toward unlubricated values (SCHMIDT13 saline 0.24-0.31)

tearing.src: reflex tearing floods the film and menisci (tears.json overflow); values E
